wire.guardrails.critical_override.help.role: Settings row help for the guardrails section in the TUI and connected settings UI
wire.guardrails.critical_override.help.note: Explains a safety override. Must keep both facts: OFF refuses critical deletions outright; ON sends them to an automatic safety check (never lets them through unchecked). 'From this machine's settings' = the settings page or CLI in the same process; a file edit (including by the agent) does not count. No ICU arguments.

wire.guardrails.critical_override.label.note: Label fits the 29-cell label budget. No ICU arguments.

wire.guardrails.enabled.help.note: User guardrail rules are markdown files the user writes; the built-in dangerous-delete check is not switchable. 'dangerous-delete' is a rule identifier and stays untranslated. No ICU arguments.

wire.guardrails.enabled.label.note: Label fits the 29-cell label budget. No ICU arguments.

wire.guardrails.judge_timeout_s.help.note: The safety check is an automatic model review of a risky tool call. Fail-closed: no answer means blocked. No ICU arguments.

wire.guardrails.judge_timeout_s.label.note: Label fits the 29-cell label budget; '(s)' is seconds. No ICU arguments.

wire.guardrails.rules_dir.help.note: '*.md' is a literal file pattern and stays untranslated. No ICU arguments.

wire.guardrails.rules_dir.label.note: Label fits the 29-cell label budget. No ICU arguments.

wire.guardrails.section.description.note: One line under the section heading. 'Dangerous' means destructive, e.g. deleting important files. No ICU arguments.

wire.guardrails.section.title.note: Section heading on the settings page. No ICU arguments.
